newsitem.title: JORDAN: Netanyahu meets King Hussein in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu meets King Hussein in Jordan.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein held talks on Sunday which Jordanian officials said would be overshadowed by Israel's plans to build new homes for Jews around Arab East Jerusalem.
Netanyahu, accompanied by his wife Sara and a delegation of senior trade and security officials, was met by Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti as he alighted from his plane.
He then went by motorcade in heavy rain to King Hussein's Raghdan Palace for talks with the Jordanian monarch as a rare thunderstorm struck the Jordanian capital.
Netanyahu was making his first trip to an Arab state since Israel signed a long-delayed deal for limited Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron in January.
Jordan, which used its close ties with the Jewish state to help broker the last-minute accord on Hebron, welcomed the deal as a new start in the Middle East peace process.
But officials said Sunday's talks would be clouded by Jordan's concerns over new Israeli plans to build 6,500 new homes for Jews in East Jerusalem.
"We consider them as very dangerous, a threat not just to the Palestinian negotiations but the peace process as a whole," one official said.
"On a bilateral level...we feel there is some effort to move things ahead by (Netanyahu's) government," the offical added. "But (the Jerusalem plans) make it very difficult for us."
King Hussein warned last week against any construction in Jerusalem that might pre-empt final negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians on the status of the holy city.
Israel says the whole of Jerusalem is its indivisable capital, while Palestinians say the East Jerusalem will form the capital of a future state.
"We are always in principle against any change in the status quo that might adversely affect any final outcome of the final negotiations over Jerusalem," the king said on Thursday.
Netanyahu and King Hussein are also expected to discuss encouraging trade between the neighbouring states, which signed a 1994 peace treaty ending a 46-year state of war.
Last year Israel and Jordan signed an accord opening up cross-border trade, but businessmen say the flow of goods has been hampered by red tape and security measures at the border.

They were also due to discuss the possibility of Jordan giving refuge to Moussa Abu Marzook, a leader of the Islamic resistance movement Hamas who has been held in a New York jail since 1995 facing extradition to Israel.
Israeli officials, fearing a wave of attacks if Abu Marzook is imprisoned in Israel, have suggested he be taken to another country on condition he renounce violence.

But Abu Marzook was expelled by Jordan shortly before his arrest in New York, and officials say King Hussein "expressed reservations" about giving him sanctuary when the idea was floated by Federal Bureau of Investigations Director Louis Freeh on Friday.
